scope: Artifact files 10-verify, 11-carry-forward, 13-system-test-author and 00-intro (node-fix-bug, claude-sonnet-5-5, inline, ShipLoop 1.3.0 artifact) read against main da9e2e75 (1.5.0): generators in skills/shiploop/scripts, plus offline renders of the three packets at a short run dir (verify head 15.3 KB of 19.8 KB, carry-forward head 15.9 KB of 21.6 KB, system-test-author 14.8 KB printed whole). Also read 12-improve (the handoff between carry-forward and system-test-author).

findings.observation: All three complete calls in my scope were piped through head despite RULES 'in the foreground, unpiped': '2>&1 | head -30' (verify), '| head -12' (carry-forward), '| head -25' (into system-test-author). The model never opened verify's packet file ('Verify stage: same pattern.'), carry-forward only grepped it for 'Exit when', and the system-test-author template reached it cut inside 'system_commands: [' ('Let me see the template for this and the remaining outer stages.'). On main the printed verify head is 153 lines: duties start at line 34, 'Full packet:' is line 122, the loop command line 129, so any head -N with N<=33 shows none of them. The trace, review, knowledge-home and skill duties were skipped and no gate could see it.
findings.proposal: (a) Zero bytes: in packet_head move 'Full packet: {path}' to line 2 as 'Full packet: {path} (the duties, template and loop command are printed below; the file adds the request, the knowledge quotes and the run rules)', drop the later bare line, and change 'The duties and rules above are this stage's' to 'below'. (b) metrics.py (plan 1.3 buckets): per stage packet_file_read_before_first_edit and the count of ShipLoop verbs run through a pipe or a $VAR. (c) Only if (b) shows the pattern on the battery, a Claude-only PreToolUse deny of a piped complete/next that prints the unpiped command (a measured arm like D-28). No new RULES bullet: the existing one was ignored 3 of 3.
findings.generic_ok: Yes: line order and a metric; the hook arm is Claude-only and optional.
findings.risk: Tests pin the 'Full packet:' position (packet-recut, e2e packet anatomy, counters). A deny could make a model hang (owner rule 13), so it stays a measured arm. The artifact is a warm inline run, so a moved path may not change behaviour; a cleared model would read the packet.
findings.est_effect: 0 bytes; the effect on packet-file opens is unmeasured and (b) decides whether (c) is built.

For one step in one item the skill recipe (duty 3 is 3,301 chars, steps 3.3-3.7 are 2,165) cannot apply by its own rule: 'update or create only when the same procedure ran in two or more steps or items'. The script knows both facts (state work_items, work_index, the step plan's steps). The artifact took 2 calls, chose none, and wrote a one-line -skill-trial.md only because WORK orders it. The recipe also lives in references/testing-and-documentation.md#reusable-product-skills. Carry-forward's merged head (18,183 at 163 chars) is one the plan says cannot hold the 4,416-char card.
findings.proposal: When no item is pending and the item has one step in a one-item run, print instead of items 2 and 3: '2. **Queue** (Carry-forward mapping guidance). No item follows <item>: omit work_items. To add a corrective item (a defect in completed work, or a prerequisite that new evidence shows missing) give work_items: the whole future queue, rows {"id", "title", "context"}, and say why in the summary.' and '3. **Skill decision**, in skill: this run has 1 step in 1 item and no pending item, so no procedure repeated. Inspect the repository skill index (HOME/environment.md ## Skills) and your host's skills and list them in evidence_refs, then record none, or reuse naming the skill in reason. WORK['carry-forward'] becomes 'Do duty items 1-3 of {run}/packets/{action}.md; for update or create, write the skill trial to {run}/notes/{action}-skill-trial.md.' A run with 2+ steps, 2+ items or a pending item keeps today's text.
findings.generic_ok: Yes: derived from counts in state, no domain words.

The owner asked on 2026-10-11 for the skill how-to to be clear, so it stays in full wherever repeat evidence is possible and as the guidance anchor otherwise. findings.where: shiploop_knowledge_home (CLOSES, STAGE_FILES, check, section_notices); shiploop_prompts.DUTIES['carry-forward'] item 1
findings.observation: Carry-forward's first duty is its only durable output: 'HOME/environment.md ## Commands: every command that worked.' Nothing checks it: CLOSES lists only prepare, release-plan and release-verify, and knowledge.check returns '' for any other stage unless the model changed HOME. In the artifact the model wrote no HOME file, assumptions [], skill none, 'The queue is empty', and ShipLoop accepted. The first possible refusal for a missing environment.md is release-plan, four stages later, when a cleared model must rebuild the commands from step-plan results. The script already knows the commands that passed: RUN/tests/<verify action>-verify1.md, runs[].command.
findings.proposal: Print one derived line under duty 1, built from that record and a substring search of HOME/environment.md: 'Commands that passed at verify and are not named in HOME/environment.md: <list | none>. Write each under ## Commands, or say in the summary why one does not belong.' (when none: 'Every command that passed at verify is already named in HOME/environment.md.'). Then report the same condition as a counted 'ShipLoop knowledge notice: ... (this close is accepted)' at carry-forward complete (a notice, not a refusal) and decide on a gate only from the notice counts.
findings.generic_ok: Yes: reads the run's own records and one living file.
findings.risk: Mention by substring is weak evidence (fine for a notice). A seeded or first-item home prints the full list. No refusal (owner rule 13, KISS).
findings.est_effect: About +200 chars (offset by VR-2); turns 'every command that worked' from recall into a script fact before the stages that read environment.md.

findings.observation: Duty 1 says 'Take the latest done test-decision record for each relevant completed item (step-plan, test-spec or test) from state.md's accepted history', but 'Results this stage builds on' lists only the spec, test-strategy and plan results (artifact and the offline render): _builds_on_lines skips the non-item: name 'test-spec' because current_actions(state) has no (None, 'test-spec'). The records are one lookup for the script (current_actions(state)[(item, stage)]), yet a cleared model must open state.md and walk history. Only test_cases and open items arrive by value. Not measured: the artifact stops at 0 tool calls for this stage.
findings.proposal: For an outer stage whose duty names per-item test decisions (system-test-author; check system-test and product-acceptance), add per completed item, via _item_actions: '<item> step-plan result: RUN/results/<id>.md (the steps, criteria, test commands, expectations and paths)', '<item> test-spec result', '<item> test result' and '<item> test candidate run: RUN/tests/<id>-verifyN.md (each command's result and count)'. In duty 1 replace "from state.md's accepted history with the locators it kept" and the replan sentence with 'The records listed above are the ones in force.' Also give the empty-use 'loop receipt' row of _PRODUCTS['test'] a use or drop it: a receipt is a 5-6 KB JSON the model has no reason to open.
findings.generic_ok: Yes: a lookup over state history.
findings.risk: About +330 chars per completed item; the head rule needs an offset (the replaced words, ~300 chars, cover one item). With many items list the last item's rows in the head and the rest in the file, naming RUN/state.md as the fallback. Confirm which outer duties really name per-item records before adding rows.
findings.plan_ref: per-packet row 16 ('records in force by script'), 2.2
findings.est_effect: About -300 chars of duty prose and +330 chars per completed item; removes a state.md walk (not measured).

findings.where: shiploop_prompts.DUTIES['verify'] items 1 and 11; shiploop_test_loop.verify(count=False) and check_only_path
findings.observation: Duty 1 says 'Run every recorded command (the Test rerun list); write each exit code and test count in RUN/notes/<action>.md' and duty 11 asks the summary for 'each command with its exit code', yet Checked-by says ShipLoop's run record is the evidence and the notes file is optional. complete --check-only already lints and reruns every recorded command and writes RUN/tests/<action>-check-only.md. In the artifact the same three commands ran in verify by the model, by check-only and by the counted complete (-verify1.md), after the test stage's own candidate run; each took 0.05-0.27 s there, so the cost is not measured (on a deploy-and-test suite each is a full cycle). The loop's one iteration added a git diff --stat and a one-line note, nothing the reruns had not shown.
findings.proposal: Duty 1: '1. **Run** complete --check-only after your last edit: it lints and reruns every recorded command (the Test rerun list) and writes each exit code and count to RUN/tests/<action>-check-only.md. Fix each refusal and repeat; copy no exit code into notes or the summary.' Duty 11: '**Summary:** entry points traced, each trace that found an issue and its fix, any required check not run and why, known limitations.' Script-checkable today: lint, rerun with floors and IDs on the final tree, the loop receipt, the item commit. Model-judged: items 2-7 and 9. The runtime's exit_checks (0.8.3) would add nothing for clause 2, because complete reruns on the final tree.
findings.risk: Plan section 10 says no effort on verify wording (0 to 1% measured): this moves two duties to records the script already writes and is not brevity, so ship it with VR-6 or not at all. The model sees refusals, not full command output, but can run one command to debug. About 230 pins.
findings.est_effect: Removes 1 of 3 verify-stage reruns and the exit-code copying; +140 / -45 chars; time unmeasured (about 0.5 s in this artifact).

findings.where: shiploop_loops.WORK['verify']; shiploop_prompts.DUTIES['verify'] intro and item 8; stage_spec verify goal
findings.observation: Three contradictions in one packet. (1) WORK and the intro say items 1-7, but exit clause 4 ('later-phase checks are marked pending with their owner') is item 9; the artifact submitted assumptions [] having read none of it. (2) Item 8 'Assembly' is a no-op on the inline route (2026-10-10 diagnosis: 'Inline, one worktree: a no-op') yet prints for it (224 chars). (3) Goal and items 1 and 4 require 'notes in RUN/notes/<action>.md' while the pass-log line says 'optional, never a completion gate'.
findings.proposal: WORK['verify'] = 'Do duty items 1-9 of {run}/packets/{action}.md in order; the review gate needs one complete iteration that finds only trivial issues.' Intro: 'Each review iteration does items 1-7 in order; items 8-9 once, before you report the exit satisfied.' Print item 8 only when delegation is ask-agent (prompt(stage, delegation=...)). Goal: '... trace entry points; review the diff; pass log RUN/notes/<action>.md.'
findings.risk: Never renumber duty items (pins, loops.WORK). A WORK edit changes contracts written after the release only. Item 8 on ask-agent keeps its text.
findings.plan_ref: 8.1 (Work lines citing only part of the duty items)
findings.est_effect: -224 chars inline; one loop-versus-exit mismatch removed.

findings.observation: commit_item returns ('', []) when changed_paths is None (no base snapshot), the same as 'no changes', so _item_commit prints nothing. In the artifact (a seeded run; verify said 'No change inventory recorded for W1') the item was never committed: the end-of-work Improve's git log shows only 'seed: baseline' and the knowledge commit, and git status shows both product files modified. Carry-forward's row 'W1 verify item commit: the WORKTREE commit whose subject starts 'feat: W1 '' prints unconditionally (the only _PRODUCTS locator that never checks), the model wrote 'W1 is committed', and the Improve's 'uncommitted' note did not reach the next packet. The final return commits leftovers, so no change is lost; the cost is a false statement in the packets that follow.
findings.proposal: In commit_item: 'if changed is None: raise ItemScopeError("the item's changes cannot be read (no base snapshot was captured when it started)")' so _item_commit prints its existing 'ShipLoop verify: ...' notice; make the 'item commit' locator return None when git log has no 'feat: <item> ' subject, as _preparatory does for its commit. Ship only these two lines (KISS: normal runs capture the base at item entry, so this is a seeded or recovery path).
findings.risk: A notice on a path normal runs rarely take; its stderr text can be cut by a pipe (VR-1); the locator runs git at render time (knowledge.recent_commits already does for intake).
findings.est_effect: No bytes; removes a false 'committed' claim.

findings.observation: END_REVIEW_FOCUS asks the last item's Improve to 'trace each new or changed public entry point with a valid, a boundary and an invalid input' and apply Code craft across every executed item: verify duties 4-5 again. On a one-step one-item run it reviews the same 7-line diff a third time (implement-step Improve, verify, end-of-work), and inline there is no independent reader at all. The artifact's end-of-work pass ran git log, git status and npm test, wrote 3 lines (trivial) and did not use the handoff.
findings.proposal: Do not cut yet: on ask-agent it is the only fresh reader. Measure: report per one-item run whether end-of-work pass 1 was trivial with an unchanged tree (the 6.4 stop rule already ends it there). If that holds in every one-item run, scope its focus by script fact to what changed after verify's commit (HOME, the skill, anything unreviewed) and say so in the opening.
findings.risk: A scoped focus could drop the cross-item view a multi-item run needs: apply only when the item count is 1.
findings.est_effect: No bytes; the stop rule bounds the cost to one pass.

works_well: ShipLoop's script-owned verify gates bind the one exit clause that can be proven: complete_runs=('loop-terminal','lint-gate','test-rerun') reruns every recorded command on the final tree with IDs and floors, then ShipLoop commits the item (shiploop_navigator._item_commit); 4 of 4 node cases passed verify and carry-forward on the first submission (LEARNINGS, 'The 8-stage inner loop in four live step slices', 2026-10-10).

Verify's whole-diff review is the only review of the test and document edits: an Improve follows step-plan, test-spec, each implement step and the last carry-forward, while test, document and verify have none. Keep it (stage_spec develop: 'what the per-step reviews could not see').
Checked by is honest about what is judged: 'ShipLoop's run record is the evidence, so a criterion is confirmed by its passing command, not by the result's summary'; 'It does not judge the work'.

complete --check-only is a non-counting preview that runs lint and the rerun (tests/<action>-check-only.md) and states 'every script gate ... accepts this result'; the artifact used it correctly before the real complete.

HEAD_END ('=== end ShipLoop head ===') lets the harness tell a cut print; packets.py labels 'the model may also have cut its output'. RESUME_LINE and the pass-log pointer ('after a reset, open it first if it exists') are sound S-6 recovery for a loop or stage lost mid-way.

The skill decision is checked structurally (SKILL.md exists with name and description) and the owner's 2026-10-11 ask for a clear how-to is met in the packet; system-test-author already carries test_cases and open items by value and has a replan route back to INNER.
not_measured: System-test-author's behaviour: the artifact stops at 0 tool calls there, so the reads a cleared model needs to find the test-decision records are not measured.
Whether a cleared model reads verify's and carry-forward's duties: the artifact is a warm inline run ('same pattern'); the S-6 battery decides.
Verify's rerun cost on a slow suite: each command took 0.05-0.27 s here.
How often the skill decision is not none: no update or create found in LEARNINGS or docs, and the 2026-10-10 diagnosis calls it 'almost always not applicable', but no systematic count was made.
Whether a missing item commit happens outside seeded or recovery runs.

Sizes are from the offline render at a short run dir; the 163-char figures (verify 17,199, carry-forward 18,183) are the plan's. The artifact ran 1.3.0, whose packets were larger (verify 28,804) and printed differently from main.
